questions.text: Section A, multiple select: which are vector quantities (a velocity, b speed, c force, d energy).
questions.expected_answer:
KEY: a=T, b=X, c=T, d=X. Velocity and force are vectors; speed and energy are scalars.
Procedure: an option with neither tick nor cross counts as a cross. Let m = options matching the key.
m=4 -> +2; m=3 -> +1; m=2 -> 0; m=0 or 1 -> -1 (a real negative mark: record -1).
A completely blank question is read as all crosses (m=2 -> 0).

criteria.description: At least 3 of 4 options match the key (m>=3)
Penalty: m=0 or 1 gives -1 overall instead of the marks above

questions.text: Section A, multiple select: which are conserved in an elastic collision (a total momentum, b velocity of each body, c direction of each body, d total kinetic energy).
questions.expected_answer:
KEY: a=T, b=X, c=X, d=T. Total momentum and total kinetic energy are conserved; individual velocities and directions change.
Same procedure as A.1: blanks count as crosses; m=4 -> +2; m=3 -> +1; m=2 -> 0; m=0 or 1 -> -1 (record -1).
A completely blank question: all crosses -> m=2 -> 0.

criteria.description: At least 3 of 4 options match the key (m>=3)
Penalty: m=0 or 1 gives -1 overall instead of the marks above

questions.text: Car from rest to 20 m/s in 5 s: acceleration and distance.
questions.expected_answer:
a = (v - u)/t = 20/5 = 4 m/s^2.  s = 1/2 a t^2 = 1/2 x 4 x 25 = 50 m (or s = (u+v)t/2 = 50 m).
Whole marks only. Apply error carried forward: a correct distance from the student's own acceleration earns the distance mark.

criteria.description: Correct formula for acceleration (a = (v-u)/t) and a = 4 m/s^2
Correct formula for distance (s = 1/2 a t^2 or s = (u+v)t/2)
Distance = 50 m, with units for both answers

questions.text: 12 V across 4 ohm: current and power.
questions.expected_answer:
I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 A.  P = V I = 12 x 3 = 36 W (also accepted: I^2 R = 36 W, V^2/R = 36 W).
Whole marks only. Units are required for the last mark.

questions.text: Acceleration of a ball at the top of its flight.
questions.expected_answer:
No. The acceleration is g = 9.8 m/s^2 (about 10 m/s^2) downward throughout the flight, including at the top. Velocity is zero only for an instant while it changes direction; gravity is still acting, so the velocity keeps changing.
2 marks for stating acceleration is not zero (= g, downward); 2 marks for the explanation (gravity acts, velocity is changing even though it is momentarily zero).

criteria.description: States that the acceleration is NOT zero and equals g, directed downward
Explains: gravity still acts / velocity is changing direction though momentarily zero

questions.text: 2 kg block from 5 m height, frictionless slope, speed at the bottom.
questions.expected_answer:
Energy conservation: m g h = 1/2 m v^2, so v = sqrt(2 g h) = sqrt(2 x 10 x 5) = sqrt(100) = 10 m/s. The mass cancels.
2 marks for the energy-conservation statement (PE at top = KE at bottom); 2 marks for correct rearrangement/substitution; 2 marks for v = 10 m/s with units. Apply error carried forward for arithmetic slips.

criteria.description: States potential energy at the top equals kinetic energy at the bottom (m g h = 1/2 m v^2)
Correct rearrangement and substitution, v = sqrt(2 g h) with g = 10 and h = 5
